referenceColors.note: sampled at y=0.3*height across the 7 top bars, left to right, via a decoded frame at fixture-authoring time (both yuv420p and yuv444p checked). Small per-channel deviation from ideal 191/0 values is expected encoder/chroma-subsampling rounding -- assert with a tolerance (e.g. +/-10 on 8-bit, scaled proportionally for 10-/12-bit), not exact equality.

MEDIA-41/93 EOS 'let audio drain' parity -- audio track is deliberately 1s longer than video, verified via ffprobe frame/DURATION metadata at authoring time

MEDIA-89/MEDIA-37 regression: real AV1-coded video with a real audio track, decoded via libavcodec's native 'av1' decoder -- confirms CNA's unified FFmpeg decode path keeps the audio track for AV1 content (a deliberate improvement beyond FNA's own dav1dfile-based AV1 path, which is video-only). Added Phase 6 (plans/plan_media.md MEDIA-89) since the original Phase 0 fixture set used only ffv1 for pixel-accuracy testing, which cannot exercise this specific codec claim.

MEDIA-90/MEDIA-95 regression: real multi-audio-track container for VideoDecoder::SetAudioStream()/VideoPlayer::SetAudioTrackEXT() round-trip testing. Track 0 (default) is a 440Hz sine tone at 48000 Hz; track 1 is an 880Hz sine tone at 44100 Hz -- the two tracks deliberately use different sample rates so a test can confirm GetSampleRate() actually changes after SetAudioStream(1), not just that the call doesn't crash. Added Phase 6 (plans/plan_media.md MEDIA-90) -- no multi-track fixture existed in the original Phase 0 set.

MEDIA-39/40 regression: a real H264/MP4 fixture used ONLY as a base for test-time byte corruption (CorruptedMidStreamDataThrowsRatherThanSilentlyEndingCleanly in VideoDecoderTests.cpp), never decoded uncorrupted by any test. Added during the Phase 8 external-review remediation after exhaustive empirical testing (a dozen+ corruption strategies against the ffv1/Matroska fixtures above) found that Matroska's demuxer is deliberately streaming-tolerant (treats any truncated/malformed tail as clean EOF) and this build's ffv1 decoder never hard-fails on a corrupted slice's CRC mismatch even under every AV_EF_* strictness flag -- H264 is far less lenient about corrupted macroblock data and reliably produces a genuine AVERROR_INVALIDDATA from avcodec_send_packet() under AV_EF_EXPLODE, which the ffv1 fixtures could not exercise.
